question.text: How much precipitation will San Francisco International Airport record on Thanksgiving Day (November 26, 2026)?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves using the daily precipitation total reported for November 26, 2026 (Pacific local time) at San Francisco International Airport (SFO/KSFO) in the National Weather Service's daily climate report for that station, product CLISFO from the NWS San Francisco Bay Area office: https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=MTR&product=CLI&issuedby=SFO. Specifically, the resolution value is the "PRECIPITATION (IN)" block's "YESTERDAY" figure in the CLISFO report dated November 27, 2026, which summarizes November 26, 2026; the multiple-choice option whose range contains that value resolves YES (for example, a reported value of 0.32 in resolves to "0.10–0.49 in"). If the November 27, 2026 CLISFO product cannot be retrieved, or if its precipitation value is reported as missing ("MM"), the archived NWS product copy in the Iowa Environmental Mesonet text-product archive (https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/list.phtml) and/or the official daily precipitation value for station USW00023234 on 2026-11-26 in NOAA's daily climate records will be used, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) being consulted if needed.
question.fine_print: Where more than one CLISFO report dated November 27, 2026 is issued (for example an original issuance at about 1:30 a.m. PST and a later corrected/CCA reissue that same day), the last such version issued on November 27, 2026 is the one used; corrections or reissues dated after November 27, 2026 do not change the resolution. Precipitation means total liquid-equivalent precipitation in inches for the calendar day, including rainfall and the melted equivalent of any frozen or freezing precipitation; reported snow depth does not count. A report of "T" (trace) is below 0.01 in and resolves to the "0.00 in (no measurable precipitation)" option.

## 1. Resolution source

Since October 1: 2.52 in. Since January 1: 13.30 in (normal 14.24). [CLISFO](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=MTR&product=CLI&issuedby=SFO)
- The background said 0.24 in month to date as of November 12, so the November 13-15 storms have added about 2.1 in.
- The November 27 report, which decides the question, does not exist yet.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles or nearly settles the question.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16, NWS Bay Area forecast discussion: rain is clearing today. Another cold front arrives late Tuesday, November 17, with an "impactful system" Wednesday and Thursday, November 18-19. That Thursday is not Thanksgiving. The WPC gives a slight risk of excessive rain and some chance of thunderstorms. Rain tapers off Friday, November 20, and "the next system… beginning on Saturday" (November 21) is expected. The discussion does not cover November 26. [NWS AFD](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=MTR&product=AFD&issuedby=MTR)
- 2026-11-15, CPC Week-2 Hazards Outlook for November 23-29 (CPC is NOAA's Climate Prediction Center):
  - It puts a **moderate risk of heavy precipitation for northern California and southwestern Oregon on November 24-25**, plus high-elevation heavy snow and high winds. Ensemble guidance gives 40-50% odds of more than 2 in over three days.
  - On Thanksgiving itself it says: "By day 11 (Nov 26), there is good agreement in the GEFS and ECMWF ensembles favoring a westward retreat of the negative height departures over the West Coast, with precipitation tools also showing a reduction of exceedance probabilities." In other words, the storm pattern is expected to pull back offshore and heavy-rain odds drop.
  - A slight risk of heavy precipitation still covers most of California for all of November 23-29. [CPC](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/threats/threats.php)
- 2026-11-15, SFGate: back-to-back storms this week, with heavy rain, thunder and gusts up to 60 mph in the hills. [SFGate](https://www.sfgate.com/weather/article/storms-waves-bay-area-22532191.php)
- 2026-11-14, Yahoo/SF Chronicle: the NWS sees an "increased risk of heavy precipitation and strong winds Nov. 25-27". The year's first king tides could coincide with the storms. [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/weather-news/articles/bay-area-mostly-dry-weather-130000994.html)
- 2026-11-13: news reports describe a strong to "extreme" El Niño and record-warm ocean water off the California coast. [NBC Bay Area](https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/local/california-ocean-temperature-records/4175530/)

## 4. Base rates
- In 1991-2020, measurable rain fell on about 1 Thanksgiving in 4 in San Francisco. It is "a little more likely" in El Niño years. Downtown San Francisco was dry every Thanksgiving from 2020 to 2025. Holiday rain tends to be light and clears within 12 to 24 hours. [SFBayWeather](https://www.sfbayweather.com/learn/thanksgiving-weather-san-francisco)
- By late November, SFO's daily chance of measurable rain is about 24% (Weather Spark, cited in the background).
- I could not find a year-by-year table of SFO Thanksgiving rain totals. The daily amounts are right-skewed: most wet days get under 0.5 in.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, "Where will it rain on Thanksgiving?", prices as of 2026-11-16 13:34 UTC: **San Francisco Yes 0.37**, San Jose 0.46, Ontario CA 0.43. I did not check which station or threshold Kalshi uses to settle; it is likely more than 0 in, which would match "anything other than 0.00/T" here.
- Kalshi, "Rain in San Francisco in Nov 2026": above 5 in at 0.85, above 6 in at 0.65, above 7 in at 0.34. The market expects a very wet rest of the month, but that says little about one specific day.
- I found no Polymarket or Manifold market for this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- November 17-20: a front and the November 18-19 system, possibly with thunderstorms. Rain then is irrelevant to the answer but shows how the pattern is behaving.
- About November 21-22: the next system.
- Daily CPC 6-10 and 8-14 day outlooks and hazards updates, and WPC days 3-7 outputs from about November 19 onward. The key question is the timing of the November 24-25 atmospheric river and whether rain after the front lingers into November 26.
- NWS Bay Area forecast discussions (about every 6-12 hours) and the point forecast for SFO, which will start showing November 26 rain chances about seven days ahead, around November 19.
- 2026-11-27, about 1:30 a.m. PST: the CLISFO report that settles the question, plus any correction issued later that day.

# SFO precipitation on Thanksgiving Day (Nov 26, 2026): research notes

The setup is a wet pattern over the West Coast. But the ensembles put the heaviest rain on Nov 24-25 and show it easing by Nov 26. Thanksgiving is about 10 days out, so no short-range rain forecast covers it yet.

## 1. Resolution source

Yesterday's weather included heavy rain. [CLISFO](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=MTR&product=CLI&issuedby=SFO)
- The resolving value is the "YESTERDAY" precipitation figure in the CLISFO dated Nov 27, 2026. That report does not exist yet.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles or nearly settles the question. Thanksgiving is 10 days away.
- The question's background said SFO had 0.24 in month to date as of Nov 12. Since then the month total has risen to 2.35 in after the Nov 13-15 storms, so the "dry season so far" framing is out of date.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16 (NWS Bay Area forecast discussion, 4:14 AM PST):
  - Rain is clearing today.
  - Another cold front arrives late Tue Nov 17, with an "impactful system" Wed-Thu Nov 18-19. It brings possible thunderstorms and a WPC slight risk of excessive rainfall.
  - Rain tapers off Fri Nov 20, and the next system brings rain "beginning on Saturday" Nov 21.
  - Temperatures stay cooler than normal throughout. Note that the "Thursday" in this discussion is Nov 19, not Thanksgiving. [NWS forecast discussion](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=MTR&product=AFD&issuedby=MTR)
- 2026-11-15 (CPC US Hazards Outlook for Nov 23-29):
  - Moderate risk of heavy precipitation for northern California and SW Oregon, and moderate risk of high winds, on Tue-Wed Nov 24-25. Both ensembles show 40-50% chances of 3-day totals above 2 in for northern California.
  - "By day 11 (Nov 26), there is good agreement in the GEFS and ECMWF ensembles favoring a westward retreat of the negative height departures over the West Coast, with precipitation tools also showing a reduction of exceedance probabilities." Negative height departures here means the trough of low pressure aloft, so it is pulling back offshore.
  - A slight risk of heavy precipitation still covers much of California for the whole of Nov 23-29. [CPC Hazards](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/threats/threats.php)
- 2026-11-15 (CPC 6-10 and 8-14 day outlooks): Above-normal precipitation is favored on the West Coast for Nov 21-25 and Nov 23-29. Confidence is above 60% for coastal central and northern California in the 6-10 day outlook, and above 50% in the 8-14 day outlook. A powerful trough sits offshore, and CPC flags uncertainty about how close to the coast it will come. [CPC](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/610day/fxus06.html)

- 2026-11-13: NBC Bay Area reports record ocean warmth off California during an "extreme El Niño" (Daniel Swain). [NBC Bay Area](https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/local/california-ocean-temperature-records/4175530/)

## 4. Base rates
- The daily chance of measurable rain at SFO in late November is about 22-24%, which implies roughly 76-78% climatological odds of 0.00 in or a trace. [Weather Spark](https://weatherspark.com/m/145212/11/Average-Weather-in-November-at-San-Francisco-International-Airport-California-United-States)

- I could not get a year-by-year list of past SFO Nov 26 totals.
- Context that cuts against pure climatology: this month is already running 3x normal, a strong El Niño is in place, and the pattern is active.

(b) **Status quo:** On any given day, SFO most often records no measurable rain, even in late November (about 76% of days are dry). With nothing changed, the answer would be "0.00 in".

(c) **Base rates:**
- Climatological chance of measurable rain on a late-November day at SFO is about 24%.
- Measurable rain fell on about 1 Thanksgiving in 4 over 1991-2020.
- Given measurable rain, rough split: about 40% fall in 0.01-0.09 in, about 40% in 0.10-0.49 in, about 13% in 0.50-0.99 in, and about 7% at 1 in or more.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- 2026-11-15, CPC Week-2 hazards: moderate risk of heavy precipitation in NorCal on November 24-25. For November 26, GEFS and ECMWF ensembles agree the trough retreats westward and exceedance probabilities fall. A slight risk still covers November 23-29.
- 2026-11-14, NWS via SF Chronicle: increased risk of heavy rain and wind on November 25-27.
- Strong El Niño and a very active pattern; November month-to-date rainfall is already 2.35 in.
- 2026-11-10, Fox Weather: models show a wet pattern on November 26-27.
- 2026-11-16, Kalshi "Rain in SF on Thanksgiving": Yes at 0.37. The threshold is likely above 0 in, which matches "anything but 0.00/T" here. This is a reasonably close anchor for P(measurable).

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** The November 24-25 atmospheric river slows by 24-36 hours, as AR timing often slips at day 9-10. Its core then lands on SFO on Thanksgiving, giving more than 1 in. Alternatively, the ridge builds faster and the whole week dries out.

**Reasoning:** I start from the 24% base rate. I adjust upward for the El Niño-driven active pattern and the NWS signal for November 25-27, and partly back down for the CPC's expectation of a retreat on day 11. That gives about 40% measurable, slightly above Kalshi's 0.37. In a wet regime, the split given rain shifts somewhat toward larger amounts. Post-frontal showers following the November 24-25 storm would most often produce light totals.
